_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Product Backlog
summary: The Product Backlog contains the complete set of prioritized Epics, Features, and User Stories with bi-directional traceability to the program requirements and highlights known work yet to be completed.
use_relationship:
The Product Backlog contains the complete set of prioritized Epics, Features, and User Stories with bi-directional traceability to the program requirements and highlights known work yet to be completed. The Product Backlog is a key product to manage development when using Agile methodologies.

The Product Backlog can be used in conjunction with the Product Roadmap (DI-IPSC-82297). The Product Roadmap shows the strategy used to drive the priorities in the Product Backlog. When both the Product Backlog and the Product Roadmap are requested in the Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL), they present a coordinated representation of the needed development for the software or system.

This DID contains the format, content, and intended use information for the data deliverable resulting from the work task described in the solicitation.

preparation_instructions.title: Reference Documents.
preparation_instructions.content: The applicable issue of the documents cited herein, including their approval dates and dates of any applicable amendments, notices, and revisions, shall be as specified in the contract.

preparation_instructions.title: Format.
preparation_instructions.content: The Product Backlog shall be in the form of an output exported from the agile management tool, including attributes such that the Government has the ability to edit, copy, and search the Product Backlog content.

preparation_instructions.title: Content.
preparation_instructions.content: The Product Backlog shall be organized in a hierarchy where Epics are decomposed into Features and Features are decomposed into User Stories with bi-directional traceability between each level. Epics are a set of features to provide a needed capability. Features are a capability or service that fulfills a stakeholder need. User Stories are the smallest unit of requirements, written from a user's perspective, describing how the software or system will be used. The Product Backlog shall include the following items:

children.title: A prioritized list of the following:
Features.
children.content: Each feature shall include a benefit hypothesis and acceptance criteria to be delivered in a Build. A Build is defined as a testable, integrated subset of the overall capability, which, together with clearly defined decision criteria, ensures adequate progress is being made before fully committing to subsequent builds in accordance with Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 5000.02, Operation of the Defense Acquisition System, 5.c.(3)(c). (Copies of DoDI 5000.02 can be obtained at: https://www.esd.whs.mil/.)

children.title: User Stories.
children.content: User Stories shall include the contents specified in Table 1 below with items a-h being required elements and items i-n being included as applicable.

children.title: Technical Stories.
children.content: A Technical Story, also known as an Enabler, identifies important algorithms, architecture, or infrastructure needed to deliver future user value. Technical Stories shall contain the contents as specified in Table 1 above, except for (a), as a Technical Story can take any format.

children.title: Defects.
children.content: Any condition that deviates from defined expectations (e.g., requirement specifications, architectures, design documents, user manuals, plans, procedures, reports, standards, policy) or suitability (e.g., from a user's or other stakeholder's sound engineering judgment or experiences). Defects can be found during the review, test, analysis, integration, or use of products, or in any of the applicable documentation. Defect is synonymous with anomaly, discrepancy, error, fault, failure, incident, flaw, problem, gripe, glitch, or bug.

children.title: Technical Debt.
children.content: Rework that needs to be done by the development team as an easier, short-term solution was pursued, yet further changes are needed for improved rigor and resiliency of subsequent developments.

children.title: The status of development shall be shown by denoting the completion of Epics, Features, User Stories, Technical Stories, Defects, and Technical Debt against the Definition of Done. The Definition of Done is an agreed upon checklist of the work that the development team is expected to finish successfully before declaring the work ready for delivery. The status of development shall also include the following:
Status for each item (e.g., Epic, Feature, User Story, Technical Story, Defect, and Technical Debt) showing either when the item was completed, or, if known, when the work is planned to be performed.
Development progress profile (e.g., percent of work complete, cumulative backlog items, release burndown).
Software productivity (e.g., velocity in story points per sprint, cumulative workflow).
Software quality and defect rates (e.g., defects per 1000 lines of code, test coverage).
All items in the Product Backlog shall contain the following configuration control information:
Record of all changes, including timestamp (date and time) when changes were made and identity of who made the changes.
Record of approval, if required, for item changes, including timestamp (date and time) when approval occurred and identity of who approved.
Record of new items added, including timestamp (date and time) when addition occurred and identity of who added the item.
Record of removal of an item, including timestamp (date and time) when removal occurred, identity of who removed the item, and rationale for removal.
